title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
layout_note: A tall vertical stack read top to bottom: image stack -> FiLM EfficientNet (MBConv blocks interleaved with FiLM rows) -> Linear 1x1 Conv -> token grid -> TokenLearner -> tokenized inputs -> positional encoding -> Transformer self-attention layers -> action token row -> output robot photo. The instruction and Universal Sentence Encoder sit in a left column whose 512-d embedding feeds every FiLM row by horizontal lines. A right column of grey annotation text (name + hyper-parameters) runs alongside each stage, tied by vertical span brackets.
grouping: The per-image vision tower is drawn as a stack of offset rounded rectangles (one per frame, 6 images), holding the MBConv/FiLM stack and TokenLearner; Tokenized Inputs, Transformer and Action are separate rounded boxes below it. Stage names and parameter counts live in a right-hand text column with thin vertical range bars marking which part of the stack each label covers.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded bars in a different pastel per MBConv block (orange, cream, green, lavender), a coral Linear 1x1 Conv bar, light-blue Self-Attention bars, and a bright blue rounded Universal Sentence Encoder box; tokens are small rounded squares (coral for vision tokens, light blue for text, green for actions); the 9x9 token grid is a dotted square, FiLM operations are grey circled dot/plus glyphs with typeset (1+gamma) and beta; positional encoding is a circled sine-wave icon.
proposed_highlight: No single module is singled out: the whole pipeline is the method, named stage by stage in large right-column headings (FiLM EfficientNet-B3, TokenLearner, Transformer, Action) with their sizes underneath; the language path is the only saturated blue box.
lesson: For a tall single-path model, put the stage names and their hyper-parameters in a right-hand text column with vertical span brackets, keeping the drawing itself to coloured bars and token rows.
notes: venue = arXiv (remembered venue: RSS 2023; first page says 'Preprint'); year = arXiv preprint year. Fig 1 is a three-part high-level overview (architecture, dataset, evaluation); Fig 3 is the architecture diagram carded here. Input and output are real robot-camera photos.

taxonomy.note: adapter-conditioning here = FiLM layers conditioning the image backbone on the sentence embedding; rl-offline = imitation learning from demonstrations

core.what: one vertical tower read top to bottom: image history and instruction -> FiLM EfficientNet -> 9x9 vision-language tokens -> TokenLearner -> 48 tokenized inputs -> decoder-only Transformer -> 11-D discrete action -> robot photo

relations.form: a single top-to-bottom column, each stage named in large type in a right-hand text column with its sizes and parameter counts beneath
the 512-d Universal Sentence Encoder embedding runs down a pale-blue bus on the left and branches right into every (1+γ)·+β FiLM layer between the MBConv blocks
the image card and the EfficientNet/TokenLearner frame are drawn as a stack of offset copies with a 'Time' arrow, one per history image, whose outputs join into one token row
tokens are drawn as their structure: a 9x9 grid of dots, 8 small grid tiles for TokenLearner, then rows of pink squares for 8 and 48 tokens
a sine-wave glyph adds positional encoding to the token stream at a circled + from the right
repeated MBConv/FiLM pairs and self-attention layers are shown as two or three copies with vertical ellipses, scope marked by grey brackets on the right

channels.colour: pink/red = tokens (linear 1x1 conv output, token rows); blue = both the language side (instruction, encoder, 512 bus) and the Transformer's self-attention blocks; green = action; the MBConv blocks each take a different colour (orange, yellow, green, purple) that encodes nothing keyed
channels.shape: rounded bars = layers, small squares = tokens, real photos = observations, circled glyphs = FiLM/positional ops
channels.line: thin pale-blue lines for the conditioning bus, grey/pink arrows for the main flow; grey brackets mark the extent of each named stage
channels.frame: a stacked rounded frame = per-image vision backbone; thin outlined boxes = token rows and action vector

quality.strengths: language conditioning arrives on its own side bus and enters each FiLM layer at the block that uses it; tokens and actions are drawn as data with their counts; the image history is shown by stacked copies rather than a label; the right-hand text column keeps sizes out of the blocks
quality.weaknesses: blue means both 'language' and 'Transformer layer'; the four MBConv colours are decorative; the FiLM backbone takes nearly half the height although it is the pretrained part; parameter counts and specs crowd the right column

insights.structure: One vertical column holds the whole policy, with the per-frame vision tower drawn as a stack of offset rounded cards, the language encoder parked in a narrow left column, and a right column of headings plus hyper-parameter text bracketed to each stage.
insights.data: The instruction is quoted text above a row of light-blue word tokens, the input and output are real robot-camera photos (a stacked six-frame input at top, a single gripper photo at bottom), and intermediates are rows of small coloured token squares (coral vision, green action) and a 9x9 dotted token grid.
insights.emphasis: Emphasis is by naming rather than highlighting: each stage gets a large right-column title with its parameter count, and FiLM conditioning is shown by repeating the typeset (1+gamma) . + beta row after every MBConv bar.
insights.flow: Data runs straight down the centre with short arrows, the sentence embedding branches out of the left column as thin horizontal light-blue lines into each FiLM row, and six pink arrows fan the per-frame tokens into the concatenated token row.
insights.avoid: The right-column text is a dense list of hyper-parameters in small grey type (pixel sizes, block counts, parameter counts) that competes with the diagram and would not survive scaling to one column.

arrangement.units: one tall column: a stacked set of rounded cards for the per-frame FiLM-EfficientNet + TokenLearner tower, then separate rounded boxes for tokenized inputs, Transformer and Action, with a left column for the instruction encoder and a right column of text annotations
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of six real robot-camera frames (top right) and a quoted instruction sentence in a rounded box (top left)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the Action box of discrete action tokens ends at a real output photo
arrangement.shared: the per-frame image tower is drawn once as a stack of offset copies (one per frame)

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
